title: Final consonants
subtitle: 받침
review: Written by Claude. The Korean and the romanization have not been checked by a Korean speaker. No audio yet: the Korean voice is not chosen.
intro: A Korean syllable can end in a consonant, written at the bottom of its block. At the end of a word it is not released: the mouth closes and stops there, with no puff of air and no extra vowel.

groups.title: k, t, p: stop, do not release
notes: Say English 'book', but stop before the k opens. Do not add a vowel: bap, not ba-pu.
Several letters are said t at the end of a word: 옷 ends in the letter s and 꽃 in ch, but both end in the sound t.

groups.title: m, n and ng
notes: These three are hummed through the nose. The letter ㅇ is silent at the start of a syllable and ng at the end of one.

groups.title: l
notes: At the end of a syllable ㄹ is a clear l, with the tip of the tongue touching just behind the top teeth.
